caption.scope: Only requests that reached the router are counted. Requests rejected before reaching the router are not included.
caption.unmetered: {count, plural, one {# unmetered call: its stream ended before usage arrived. It is not in the cost above. Approximate upper bound: {upperBound}.} other {# unmetered calls: their streams ended before usage arrived. They are not in the cost above. Approximate upper bound: {upperBound}.}}
caption.unmetered.help: The bound is approximate: the estimated prompt at the uncached input price, plus the requested output cap at the output price. The prompt is estimated at 4 characters per token, so the bound can be too low for Chinese, Japanese or Korean text.
caption.unmetered.partial.help: Some of these calls set no output cap, so their bound covers input only. The total may be well below the real cost.
caption.listPrice: List price from the {region} price catalog {catalogVersion}. This is not your AWS invoice: discounts, credits and taxes are not included.
caption.retention: Request records are kept {days} days. Daily totals are kept {rollupDays} days.
caption.noContent: Prompt and output text are never stored.
term.tier: Tier: fast, standard or frontier. Each tier maps to models in the routing policy.
term.observe: Observe: the router serves a fixed default model and only logs what it would choose.
term.auto: Auto: the router serves the model it chooses.
term.session: Session: one agent session, identified by its session header. Shown as a short label, never the raw id.
term.lineage: Lineage: one agent's chain of requests in a session. Sub-agents get their own lineage.
term.breakPoint: Cache break point: a moment when the prompt cache is cold anyway (session start, sub-agent start, idle past the TTL, compaction). The router switches models only at these points.
term.hardLock: Hard lock: the router keeps the current model (tool loop, response chain, or state another model cannot read).
term.costGate: Cost gate: a downgrade must save more over the next calls than the cold write it causes.
term.coldWrite: Cold write: writing the whole context into the cache of a new model after a switch.
term.hitRate: Cache hit rate: cache read tokens divided by prompt tokens.
term.listPrice: List price: the price in the region's price catalog. Not your invoice.
term.baseline: Baseline: what the same tokens would cost on a fixed choice of model.
term.caller: Caller: the member or service client that sent the request.
term.unattributed: Unattributed: the request had no valid identity header, so the router could not tell who sent it.
term.pin: Pin: the client asked for a specific model with x-router-hint: pin=<model id>.
term.failover: Failover: the router retried on another inference profile or a sibling model after an error.
term.fallback: Legacy gateway fallback configuration is shown read-only on Gateway. New deployments route only to the router and fail closed when it is unavailable.
term.assessor: Assessor: an optional LLM that proposes a tier for a turn. In observe mode its answer is only logged.
term.pack: Pack: the assessor's prompt and rules, bundled in the router image.
term.wouldChoose: Would choose: the model auto mode would have served. Logged in observe mode.

savings.title: Savings
savings.description: What routing changed in list-price cost, against a baseline.
savings.baseline.static.help: Each request is priced on the model of the tier it asked for: auto uses the pool's default tier, auto:fast uses fast. Tiers the client chose itself save nothing.
savings.baseline.frontier.help: Frontier baseline: the same token counts at the frontier model's list price. In our coding-agent benchmarks frontier solved no more tasks than standard (Opus 5.5 about 2.5 times Sonnet 5.5's cost, GPT-6 Astra about 5–6 times Sol's), so this saving is a price gap, not a saving at equal quality.
savings.baseline.observeDefault.help: In observe mode this equals actual, so the net saving is minus the assessor overhead.
savings.baseline.help: A baseline prices the same requests on one fixed model that never switches, from the same API's pool.
savings.baseline.fallback: {dialect}: the current pool has no {tier} model, so this baseline prices its requests on {model} ({modelTier}).
savings.baseline.fallbackNone: {dialect}: the current pool has no model for this baseline, so its requests have no baseline price.
savings.baseline.missing: {count, plural, one {# request has no price on this baseline and is left out of these figures.} other {# requests have no price on this baseline and are left out of these figures.}}
savings.kpi.routing.help: R = B − A*: the price difference between the baseline model and the served model, with cold-cache effects removed.
savings.kpi.switchPenalty.help: S = A − A*: extra cache writes when routing moved a warm lineage to another model.
savings.kpi.assessor.help: X: what the assessor's own calls cost.
savings.kpi.netFormula: Net saving N = B − A − X = R − S − X
savings.kpi.cache.help: Cnet: what the same tokens would cost with no caching, minus actual cost, net of the cache-write premium. This comes from prompt caching, not from routing.
savings.matrix.title: Where requests went
savings.matrix.help: Requests by baseline tier and served tier, with their routing effect.
savings.matrix.helpProjected: Requests by baseline tier and the tier auto would choose, with their routing effect.
savings.otherCold.help: Cache writes after switches that routing did not choose: failover, a policy change, a client pin. Not in the net saving.
savings.capRow.help: Requests served at a lower tier because of a tier limit. A forced downgrade is not a routing saving, so it is shown on its own.
savings.tab.projectedAssessed: Projected if auto, with the assessor's proposals (indicative)
savings.projected.count: {count, plural, one {# request where auto would have chosen another model} other {# requests where auto would have chosen another model}}
savings.projectedAssessed.missing: {count, plural, one {# request has no assessed projection (logged before the router recorded it) and is left out.} other {# requests have no assessed projection (logged before the router recorded it) and are left out.}}
savings.projectedAssessed.changed: {count, plural, one {# request where the assessor's proposal changes auto's choice} other {# requests where the assessor's proposal changes auto's choice}}
savings.caption.listPrice: All figures are list prices ({catalogVersion}), not your invoice.
savings.caption.sameUsage: Same usage is assumed: the baseline prices the same token counts at the baseline model's price. A different model may use more or fewer tokens and turns.
savings.caption.quality: Quality is not measured. A cheaper model may solve fewer tasks. In our coding-agent benchmarks the fast tier solved 14–17 points fewer tasks than standard.
savings.caption.observe: Observe mode: the router serves the observe default, so the figures show only how that model differs from the baseline. "Projected if auto" estimates what auto would have cost.
savings.caption.projection: Indicative, not measured: the same tokens repriced on the models auto would have chosen, carried forward along each lineage. Exact for the shipped policy; approximate when user turns are cost-gated.
savings.caption.projectionAssessed: Indicative, not measured: the same tokens repriced on the models auto would choose if the assessor's proposals were applied, carried forward along each lineage. Where the assessor made no proposal, auto's choice is kept.
savings.caption.evidence: Benchmark evidence: on two coding benchmarks, auto with the assessor cost 2.6–4.1 times fixed standard, with no quality gain detected.
savings.caption.unmetered: {count, plural, one {# unmetered call is left out of these figures.} other {# unmetered calls are left out of these figures.}}
savings.empty.observeBaseline: With the observe default as baseline in observe mode, actual equals baseline. The net saving is minus the assessor overhead. Open "Projected if auto" or pick another baseline.

decision.assessor.packText: Rule text from the pack, not translated.

getStarted.title: Get started
getStarted.intro: Connect your coding agent or your code to the router. You sign in with your own account. No shared secret and no AWS credentials are needed.
getStarted.values.title: This deployment
getStarted.values.missing: This deployment is not fully configured. Ask an admin.
getStarted.values.missingAdmin: Missing value: {name}. Set it in the stack and deploy again.
getStarted.step1.title: 1. Install llmar
getStarted.step1.body: llmar is one Python 3 file with no dependencies outside the standard library. llmar-token and llmar-login are links to it, so tools can call them with no arguments.
getStarted.step1.source: It is published in the project repository. The console does not serve files.
getStarted.configure.title: 2. Configure it for this deployment
getStarted.configure.body: This saves the deployment's values in ~/.config/llmar/config.json: sign-in domain, client id, scope, callback ports and gateway URL. The file holds no secrets.
getStarted.step2.title: 3. Sign in
getStarted.step2.body: llmar login opens your browser at the sign-in page. Sign in with your password. llmar then saves a refresh token in ~/.config/llmar/. Only you can read the file.
getStarted.step2.mfa: First sign-in: replace the temporary password from the invite e-mail with your own.
getStarted.step2.again: Sign in again after {refreshDays} days, after "Sign out everywhere", or after an admin re-enabled your account.
getStarted.step2.noBrowser: No browser on this machine (for example over SSH)? Run llmar login --no-browser. It prints a link and an ssh -L command. Forward the port, then open the link on your own computer.
getStarted.step2.test: Test: llmar status shows who you are and when your token expires.
getStarted.step3.title: 4. Set up your tool
getStarted.step3.identity: Send the token twice: as Authorization: Bearer and as x-api-key. The gateway checks the first. The router reads the second to record you as the caller.
getStarted.claudeCode.token: apiKeyHelper runs llmar-token. Claude Code sends the token as a bearer token and as x-api-key. With the TTL at 4 minutes it asks often; llmar answers from its cache and refreshes the token before it expires.
getStarted.claudeCode.tiers: The alias variables make /model opus, sonnet and haiku ask the router for a tier. Claude Code does not know the name auto; CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS gives it the 1M window of the router's Claude models, so it does not compact at its 200K default.
getStarted.claudeCode.countTokens: The gateway does not offer /v1/messages/count_tokens. Claude Code gets a 404 and uses its own estimate.
getStarted.claudeCode.refusal: If the model refuses on safety grounds, Claude Code may retry with its built-in fallback model. That id is not routable, so the retry fails.
getStarted.codex.catalog: First create a model catalog that tells Codex the context window of auto. Codex does not know auto and caps it at 272K, whatever model_context_window says. The file is a copy of the catalog shipped with Codex, plus auto with GPT-6.1 Sol's metadata and a 1M window. If your Codex version does not ship GPT-6.1 Sol, the command copies another Sol or the catalog's first model, and prints which one it copied. Run the command again after you upgrade Codex.
getStarted.codex.auth: Codex runs llmar-token for the Authorization header and refreshes it every 4 minutes. After saving the configuration, run this command to replace ~ in the auth command with your home directory; Codex does not expand it there. A home directory is typically /home/username on Linux or /Users/username on macOS, but can be different; the command uses your actual home directory.
getStarted.codex.oauth: For x-api-key, Codex signs you in a second time in its own browser window. This is how the router records you as the caller. So you sign in once to llmar and once to Codex.
getStarted.codex.ssh: Over SSH, Codex's own sign-in needs its callback port forwarded too: ssh -L {port}:127.0.0.1:{port} <host>. Codex prints the sign-in URL; open it on your own computer.
getStarted.codex.keyring: Headless Linux without a keyring: add credentials_store = "file" to the gateway_oauth table. Codex then keeps its sign-in in $CODEX_HOME/secrets/gateway_oauth.json (mode 0600, plain text).
getStarted.codex.short: Sessions shorter than 60 minutes can skip the second sign-in. Use the provider table below instead, and leave out the auth and gateway_oauth tables: one token is read at start and sent in both headers.
getStarted.codex.webSearch: Web search must stay off. With it on, Bedrock ends every stream with an error and Codex retries until it gives up.
getStarted.codex.warning: If Codex warns "Model metadata for 'auto' not found", it is not reading the catalog: check the model_catalog_json path. Without the catalog, sessions compact at about 258K tokens.
getStarted.sdk.token: RouterAuth asks llmar for a token on every request and sets both headers. llmar answers from its cache, so this is cheap, and a long-running process never sends an expired token.
getStarted.sdk.session: Use one x-router-session id per agent session. Cache-aware routing depends on it. Never share one id across sessions.
getStarted.sdk.decision: To see which model served a call, read the x-router-model response header (with_raw_response in both SDKs).
getStarted.sdk.stream: Streaming works with the SDKs' usual calls.
getStarted.curl.body: A single call to check the setup. -D - prints the response headers, including x-router-model.
getStarted.step4.title: 5. Check your setup
getStarted.step4.body: Send one request with your tool, then press Check.
getStarted.step4.found: Found your request from {time}: {dialect}, requested {requested}, served by {model}.
getStarted.step4.notFound: No request from you in the last 10 minutes. If you sent one, check that the x-api-key header is set (step 4).
getStarted.step4.require: This deployment requires your identity. A request without x-api-key gets 401 identity-missing.
getStarted.step4.observe: Without x-api-key your requests still work, but they are not recorded as yours.
getStarted.step4.off: Identity is off in this deployment, so requests are not recorded per caller and this check cannot find yours.
getStarted.models.title: Models and tiers in this deployment
getStarted.models.observe: This deployment runs in observe mode. Every auto request is served by the observe default: {observeDefaults}. Tier aliases and tier= hints take effect only in auto mode. A pin= hint works in both modes.
getStarted.models.auto: This deployment runs in auto mode. The router picks a tier for each request and switches models only at cache break points.
getStarted.endpoints.title: Endpoints and headers
getStarted.endpoints.model: Send model auto, or auto:fast, auto:standard or auto:frontier. A concrete model id is treated as a pin: it is served if it is in the routing policy and within your tier limit. Otherwise you get 400 (pin-not-allowed or access-cap).
getStarted.endpoints.headers: The gateway forwards only these request headers: {headers}.
getStarted.endpoints.response: Response headers: x-router-decision, x-router-model (the model that served the call) and x-router-reason.
getStarted.trouble.title: Troubleshooting
getStarted.trouble.401: 401: no token or an invalid one. With identity required, also a missing x-api-key (identity-missing) or an invalid one (identity-…).
getStarted.trouble.403: 403 identity-blocked: your account is disabled or blocked. Ask an admin. A 403 insufficient_scope from the gateway usually means the access token expired: send the request again (llmar hands out a new token). If it repeats, run llmar-token, then llmar login if it asks, and check the clock (date -u).
getStarted.trouble.pin: 400 pin-not-allowed: the pinned or named model is not in the routing policy.
getStarted.trouble.accessCap: 400 access-cap: the pinned model or model id you asked for is above your tier limit. A tier you ask for above the limit is not an error: you are served at the highest tier you may use. Ask an admin to raise the limit.
getStarted.trouble.accessCapContext: 400 access-cap-context: the conversation is too long for every model within your tier limit. Start a new session or compact the context.
getStarted.trouble.countTokens: 404 on count_tokens: harmless. The client uses its own estimate.
getStarted.trouble.codexStream: Codex "stream disconnected before response.completed": web search is on. Turn it off.
getStarted.trouble.relogin: "run llmar login" (llmar-token exit code 2): your sign-in expired or was revoked, or the settings changed (llmar configure) since you signed in. Run llmar login. If it keeps failing, your account may be disabled.
getStarted.trouble.codexAuth: Codex says "auth command exited with status 2" and nothing more: run llmar-token in a terminal to see why. Usually you need to run llmar login.
getStarted.trouble.idpDown: llmar-token exit code 3: the sign-in service cannot be reached and no usable cached token is left. While the cached token has more than 30 seconds left, llmar still prints it, with a warning.
getStarted.trouble.usage: llmar-token exit code 4: a setup problem, such as missing settings, a credentials file other users can read, the llmar directory or its parent writable by others, or bad usage. The message says which.
getStarted.trouble.budget: 429 budget-exceeded: you are over your monthly budget. Ask an admin.
getStarted.admin.clients: For CI and other automation, create a service client instead of using a member account.
members.title: Members
members.description: People who use the router. They sign in with their own account.
members.col.name: Name
members.invite.name: Name
members.invite.help: Cognito sends an e-mail with a temporary password. The member sets a new password at first sign-in.
members.roleApplies: The new role applies at the router within about 35 seconds.
members.adminSignIn: {name} must sign in again before the admin rights apply.
members.adminSignIn.self: You are now an admin. Sign in again to use the admin pages.
members.signOutEverywhere.confirm: This revokes {name}'s refresh tokens. Their llmar CLI and console sessions must sign in again. Tokens already issued work at the gateway until they expire (up to 60 minutes) unless you also disable the member.
members.disable.title: Disable {name}?
members.disable.body: In require mode the router stops serving {name} within about 35 seconds. In observe mode, requests that carry {name}'s identity are blocked within about 35 seconds, but requests without it are served until the token expires (up to 60 minutes). Their records stay.
members.enable.body: {name} can use the router again within about 35 seconds. They must run llmar login again, because disabling revoked their sign-in.
members.delete.title: Delete {name}?
members.delete.body: Only disabled members can be deleted. Their records stay and show as "Deleted member". This cannot be undone.
members.error.exists: A user with this e-mail already exists.
members.error.self: You cannot disable or delete your own account.
members.error.lastAdmin: This is the last admin. Make someone else an admin first.
members.empty: No members yet. Invite the first one.
budget.title: Budget
budget.hardStop: Stop serving when the budget is used up
budget.hardStop.help: The router answers 429 budget-exceeded within a few minutes after the budget is used up: usage is counted from the router logs, which arrive in batches. Requests in that window still go through, so spend can pass the budget a little. In observe mode this binds only calls that carry x-api-key. Budgets use list price, so they can differ from the invoice.
budget.advisory: In observe mode, budgets bind every call that carries a valid x-api-key. A call without one is served unattributed and escapes them. They bind everyone only in Require.
budget.spendIncludes: Budget spend is actual cost plus assessor cost, for the current UTC month.
clients.title: Service clients
clients.description: Machine callers such as CI jobs and agents. They use the client-credentials flow.
clients.col.name: Name
clients.create.name: Name
clients.limits.help: Budgets and tier limits work as for members. Without its own values, a client has no budget and no tier limit.
clients.secret.title: Client secret
clients.secret.once: Copy the secret now. It is shown only once.
clients.secret.store: Store it in a Secrets Manager secret that only this job can read. Do not put it in config files.
clients.secret.script: The machine token script from the README reads the secret and prints a token. Send it as Authorization: Bearer and as x-api-key:
clients.rotate.body: A new secret is created. Update the job before you remove the old one.
clients.disable.body: The router stops serving this client within about 35 seconds. In observe mode this holds only for calls that send x-api-key.
clients.delete.body: Records stay. This cannot be undone.
clients.empty: No service clients. Members use their own account; service clients are for automation.
config.comment.required: Say what you changed and why.
config.valid: Valid. Nothing is active until you activate it.
config.invalid: {count, plural, one {# problem} other {# problems}} found.
config.activate.title: Activate version {version}?
config.activate.body: The router picks it up within about 1 minute. Sessions keep their current model until their next cache break point.
config.effects.title: Effect on running sessions
config.effects.none: No running session changes model because of this.
config.effects.list: {count, plural, one {# change can move sessions at their next cache break point:} other {# changes can move sessions at their next cache break point:}}
config.effects.cannotCompare: The active config no longer passes validation, for example because a model left the price catalog. So the effect on running sessions cannot be computed. Check the whole change before you activate it.
config.conflict: Someone activated version {version} while you were editing. Review their change first.
config.rollback.body: This creates a new version with the content of version {version}.
config.error.universe: {model} is not in the allowed model list. Confirm it on the Models page, or widen the list with a CDK deploy (parameter allowedModelUniverse).
config.error.catalog: {model} is not in the {region} price catalog.
config.rejected: The router rejected this version and kept version {active}: {reason}
policy.title: Routing policy
policy.description: Which models serve each tier, and how the router chooses.
policy.whatIf.later: Replaying recent decisions under a draft comes in a later release.
policy.mode.help: Observe serves the observe default and logs what auto would choose. Auto serves the chosen model.
policy.autoWarning: In auto mode the router serves the model it chooses. Check the Savings projection and the benchmark evidence first.
policy.observeDefaults.help: The model that serves each API in observe mode.
policy.aliases.help: Model names clients may send, and the tier each one asks for.
policy.aliases.name: Name
policy.rules.help: Rules set the desired tier for matching requests. The first match wins.
policy.sessionTier.help: When on, the whole session takes the tier chosen at its start.
policy.portability.help: Per state tag: same-model, same-family, or strip-upgrade (openai-encrypted-reasoning only: a Codex session may move up a tier, and the router drops the earlier model's encrypted reasoning).
policy.routing.title: Routing mode
policy.routing.observe.help: Every request uses the observe model (normally the Normal one). The rest of this page only records what Auto would do.
policy.routing.auto.help: The difficulty rows and the rules below pick the model.
policy.routing.assessor: Let an AI judge each task's difficulty
policy.routing.assessor.help: A small model reads each session's task and moves it to Easy or Hard. Adds 1–3 s at session start, about $0.0007 a session.
policy.routing.assessor.observeNote: The assessor still records its opinion for the savings pages (about $0.0007 a session). Turn it off under Advanced.
policy.routing.assessor.unknown: The assessor setting is unknown; see Effective settings.
policy.routing.assessor.noPack: This deployment has no assessor pack.
policy.routing.custom.packAuto: The assessor runs at each session start but may act only through rules the pack marks for auto. Pack {pack} marks {count, plural, =0 {none, so it changes nothing} one {# rule} other {# rules}}. About $0.0007 a session.
policy.routing.custom.packAutoUnknown: The assessor runs at each session start but may act only through rules the pack marks for auto. About $0.0007 a session.
policy.routing.custom.observeAuto: Models never change. The assessor's opinion only changes what the savings pages say Auto would do.
policy.routing.choose: Choosing Observe or Auto replaces the custom setting.
policy.pools.title: Models by task difficulty
policy.pools.help: One model per difficulty. The default row serves requests that no rule or assessor moves.
policy.pools.serviceTier.help: The router asks for the {tier} service tier on this model when the client sends none.
policy.pools.cannotShow: This pool uses a layout the form cannot show: {reason}. Edit it in the JSON tab.
policy.pools.cannotShow.unknownModel: {model} is not in the price catalog for this API
policy.pools.notSetUp: Not set up: requests on this API are refused.
policy.pools.defaultEmpty: The default row is empty; {model} serves instead.
policy.pools.failover: Other entry points of the same model (usually empty)
policy.pools.failover.help: Inference profile ids of the same model in other regions, tried when this one is throttled. Comma-separated.
policy.pools.failoverOther: {id} is a different model. Put other models in their own row.
policy.pools.failoverDropped: The other entry points of the old model were removed.
policy.pools.observeOverride: Observe uses {model}, not the default row.
policy.rules.title: Rules
policy.rules.note: The first matching rule wins. Rules apply to requests for `auto`, not to `auto:fast` or a named model.
policy.rules.empty: No rules: requests for `auto` use the default row (or what the assessor picks).
policy.rules.cannotShow: These rules use a form the page cannot show; edit them in Advanced (JSON).
policy.rule.minTokens: prompt of at least {n, number} tokens
policy.rule.maxTokens: prompt of at most {n, number} tokens
policy.rule.shadowed: Never reached: rule {n} matches every request first.
policy.rule.edit.title: Rule
policy.rule.edit.listHelp: Comma-separated. End a name with * to match every name that starts with it.
policy.nl.title: Describe a rule in one sentence
policy.nl.help: An AI turns the sentence into rules for you to check. Nothing is saved until you add the rules and activate.
policy.nl.placeholder: e.g. Sub-agents use the cheap model
policy.nl.off: Natural-language rules are off in this deployment (deploy parameter rulesModel).
policy.nl.none: No rule came out of this sentence.
policy.nl.unsupported: Could not be turned into a rule
policy.nl.reason.task-content: Depends on the task in a way the assessor cannot judge from its task card.
policy.nl.reason.no-condition: No condition the router can check (session type, prompt size, model name, agent id).
policy.nl.reason.ambiguous: Not clear enough: say which requests and which difficulty.
policy.nl.reason.invalid: The result was not a valid rule.
policy.nl.added: {count, plural, one {# rule} other {# rules}} added to the draft.
policy.nl.unavailable: The translator did not answer. Write the rule with Add rule instead.
policy.summary.title: What happens now
policy.summary.help: Written by the console from this draft (not by an AI).
policy.summary.observe.serves: Every request for `auto` or another alias ({aliases}) uses {model}. Model names that are not aliases are used as sent.
policy.summary.observe.noDefault: No observe model set: requests are served as Auto would choose.
policy.summary.observe.recorded: Recorded only, what Auto would do:
policy.summary.assessor.auto: Otherwise the assessor reads the task: easy → {easy}, hard → {hard}, else {normal}.
policy.summary.assessor.observe: The assessor records its opinion only (about $0.0007 a session).
policy.summary.sessionTier: Sub-agents take the main session's difficulty.
policy.summary.pins: Other model names are used as sent (if allowed).
policy.summary.when.breaks: A session's model can change only when it or a sub-agent starts, after compaction, or after a long pause; never during a tool loop.
policy.summary.when.retain: A new user message alone never changes it; only the cases above do.
policy.summary.when.costGated: At a new user message it can also move up when needed, and down only when that saves money.
policy.summary.when.upgradeOnly: At a new user message it can also move up at once when the assessor, a rule, an alias or a hint asks for a harder tier, even though that starts a new prompt cache; it never moves down there.
policy.summary.when.codexStrip: Codex sessions can move up too: from then on the router drops the earlier model's encrypted reasoning from the history it forwards.
policy.summary.caps: Tier limits can lower this for {groups}.
policy.summary.noPools: No model pool is set up: every request for `auto` is refused.
policy.advanced.switches.help: The three settings the routing mode card sets together. Use them for combinations the card calls Custom, or to turn the assessor off.
policy.advanced.observeDefaults.help: Follows the default row unless you set another model here.
assessor.setOnRouting: Turned on and off on the Routing policy page.
assessor.state.acting: Auto mode uses it: sessions move to Easy or Hard.
assessor.state.recording: Records its opinion only; models do not change because of it.
assessor.state.link: Change on the Routing policy page
access.title: Tier limits
access.help: Limit the highest tier a group or a caller may use. Applies within about 35 seconds. It also limits the observe default, would-choose and projected models.
access.allowPins.help: Empty: a pin is allowed when its tier is within the limit. A listed model is allowed even above the limit.
access.precedence: A caller's own limit wins over the group default.
access.advisory: In observe mode, tier limits bind every call that carries a valid x-api-key. A call without one is served unattributed and escapes them.
assessor.title: Assessor
assessor.description: An optional LLM that proposes a tier at the start of a turn.
assessor.mode.help: Off: never called. Observe: called, answer only logged. Auto: the answer can change the served model.
assessor.autoWarning: In auto mode the assessor's tier changes the served model. In our benchmarks no ability to pick the tasks that need frontier was detected, and it never chose fast. Keep observe until the offline evaluation passes.
assessor.autoConfirm: I have read the evidence and want auto mode.
assessor.pack.bundled: Only packs bundled in the router image can be chosen.
assessor.threshold.help: An answer below this confidence is treated as no opinion.
assessor.autoRules: Rules that may act in auto mode
assessor.savesConfig: Saving creates a new config version. The routing policy in it is unchanged.
assessor.rules.title: Rules in {pack}
assessor.rules.textNote: Rule text is shown as written in the pack.
assessor.stats.title: Activity
gateway.title: Gateway
gateway.description: The AgentCore Gateway in front of the router. Most settings change only with a CDK deploy.
gateway.authorizer.scopesOnly: The gateway checks the token and its scope. The router checks who the caller is.
gateway.rules.all: Auto aliases and all other model names go only to the router (auto and catch-all rules).
gateway.rules.fallback: New deployments fail closed: if the router answers 5xx or cannot be reached, the request fails. The gateway does not invoke models directly.
gateway.fallbackChain.none: None — requests fail if the router is unavailable; no direct model invocation.
gateway.fallbackChain.legacy: Legacy fallback configuration read from this deployment. It is shown read-only, not as evidence that fallback served any requests.
providers.title: Providers
providers.description: Model providers besides Bedrock. Edit them here: a change is a new configuration version (validate, review, activate), like routing. Providers must lie inside the deployment's egress boundary, which only a deploy changes. Their models can be used in routing pools, not as the assessor model.
providers.none.hint: Add one with Add provider (inside the egress boundary below), or deploy with a provider registry (CDK parameter providersFile).
providers.source.baked: Deploy-time registry (CDK parameter providersFile); editing makes it part of the configuration
providers.unsaved: Unsaved changes: validate and activate to apply them.
providers.issues: {count, plural, one {# problem} other {# problems}} with this provider
providers.boundary.title: Egress boundary
providers.boundary.description: Where this deployment lets prompts go besides Bedrock. Set at deploy time and enforced by the network; the console cannot change it.
providers.form.id.help: Lowercase letters, digits and '-', up to 32 characters; not 'bedrock'. Model ids become <id>/<upstream model>. Cannot be changed later.
providers.form.id.invalid: Use lowercase letters, digits and '-' (up to 32), not 'bedrock'
providers.form.baseUrl.help: https://host[/path], no trailing '/'. Must be inside the egress boundary.
providers.form.header.help: Required for an API key header (e.g. api-key); bearer uses Authorization when empty.
providers.form.secret.managed: Stored by the console: set it on the provider card after saving.
providers.form.secret.arn: A secret the deployment provides (kept as is).
providers.form.secret.env: An environment variable (local runs only; refused by a deployed console).
providers.form.paths.help: Appended to the base URL; empty uses the default shown.
providers.form.betaDeny.help: Comma-separated beta names the provider rejects.
providers.form.usage.help: Dot path inside the usage object, when the provider reports it in a non-standard field.
providers.form.models.none: At least one model is required.
providers.model.longContext.help: JSON with aboveTokens (a token count) and price (input, output, cacheRead, cacheWrite); empty = none.
providers.key.help: Write-only: stored in Secrets Manager for the router and never shown again.
providers.key.notSet: No key yet: requests to this provider fail until one is set
providers.key.unavailable: This deployment gives the console no place to store provider keys (no provider secret prefix). Redeploy with an egress mode to manage keys here.
providers.key.failed: The key could not be saved (Secrets Manager error).
providers.key.confirm.title: Remove the key of {id}?
providers.key.confirm.body: The key is scheduled for deletion. Requests to this provider fail once the router stops using its cached key (within minutes).
providers.remove.confirm: Removing {id} also removes its models; pools that use them must change in the same activation.
health.title: Health
health.description: Is the router serving well right now.
health.tasksZero: The router has 0 tasks. Router-only deployments reject requests while it is unavailable. Check Gateway for this deployment's rules.
health.fallbackSigns.help: Router 5xx, unhealthy-target/task-count proxies, and fewer running tasks than desired indicate availability problems, not direct model invocation. Router-only deployments fail closed; check Gateway for legacy fallback configuration.
audit.title: Audit log
audit.description: Every admin action, with who, when and what changed.
audit.action.member.update: Changed a member's budget or tier limit
audit.action.config.redeliver: Republished a config version to the router
audit.action.config.translateRules: Translated a sentence into routing rules
audit.readOnly: The audit log cannot be edited.
audit.empty: No admin actions in this period.
settings.title: Settings
settings.mfa.off: Off in this deployment. For production, require TOTP MFA on the user pool. It is a stack setting: see infra/README.md, "Production hardening: MFA".
settings.signOutEverywhere.body: Signs you out of every browser and revokes your llmar CLI sign-in. The CLI notices at its next refresh, within 60 minutes, and the gateway accepts tokens already issued until they expire. Run llmar login again afterwards.
settings.signOutEverywhere.done: You are signed out everywhere, including the llmar CLI. Sign in again here, and run llmar login for your tools.
settings.identity.help: Whether the router needs to know the caller. Require rejects requests without a valid x-api-key.
settings.identity.requireWarning: Clients that do not send a valid llmar token in x-api-key will get 401. Check the Unattributed share on the Overview first.
settings.identity.observeNote: In observe mode, blocks, budgets and tier limits apply to every call that carries a valid x-api-key. A call without one is served unattributed and escapes them. They bind everyone only in Require.
settings.identity.requireBlocked: You cannot switch to Require yet. The router has not reported that its signing keys are loaded. Without them, every call would get 401.
settings.retention.help: Set at deploy time (recordRetentionDays). A change applies to new records. Daily totals are kept 400 days.
settings.defaultBaseline.help: Used on the Overview and as the Savings page's first choice. Always frontier (the default) shows what the same tokens would cost on the frontier model; Requested tier compares with the tier each request asked for, usually standard.
settings.cdkOnly: Set at deploy time. Change it with a CDK deploy.
settings.saved: Saved. It applies within about 1 minute.
auth.noRole: Your account has no role yet. Ask an admin.
ext.reload.title: A new version of the console is available
ext.reload.body: This page needs a file from the new version. Reload to continue.
ext.nav.label: Navigation
ext.configError.title: This console is not configured
ext.configError.body: The deployment's /config.json is missing or invalid. Ask an admin to redeploy the console.
ext.settings.password.help: Opens the sign-in page, where you reset your password with a code sent by e-mail.
ext.settings.retention.range: Enter a whole number from 7 to 365.
ext.source.document.title: Set in config version {version}.
ext.source.baked.title: No console config version sets this, so the router uses the value set at deploy time ({version}).
ext.source.unknown.title: The deploy defaults (config/baked.json) could not be read, so this value is not known.
ext.effective.title: Settings in effect
ext.effective.description: Each value comes from the active config version, or from the deploy default when the version does not set it.
ext.effective.unknown: Some settings are unknown because the deploy defaults (config/baked.json) could not be read. The console does not guess them. A new draft starts from the active version as written.
ext.reported.title: Reported by router tasks
ext.reported.description: The settings each running router task last reported, next to the configured ones.
ext.reported.empty: No router task has reported its settings yet.
ext.reported.mismatch: {count, plural, one {# router task reports settings that differ from the config, for example because it still runs an old image or environment.} other {# router tasks report settings that differ from the config, for example because they still run an old image or environment.}}
ext.app.mode.unknown.tooltip: The routing mode is not known: the deploy defaults could not be read.
ext.getStarted.models.unknown: The routing mode of this deployment is not known right now. Ask an admin to check Routing policy.
ext.getStarted.step4.unknown: The identity mode of this deployment is not known right now. Set x-api-key so that your requests are recorded as yours.
ext.state.configUnavailable: The deploy-time settings cannot be read. The router keeps running on its current config. Retry, or check the router stack deploy.
ext.effects.identityWeakened: The identity mode goes down. Calls without a valid x-api-key will be served, and blocks, budgets and tier limits will not apply to them. In Off, they apply to no call.
ext.effects.identityStrengthened: The identity mode goes up. In Require, a call without a valid x-api-key gets 401. Check the unattributed share on the Overview first.
ext.effects.assessorMode: The assessor mode changes. In Auto, the assessor's tier can change the served model; in Observe or Off, it cannot.
ext.identityKeys.count: {total, plural, one {Signing keys loaded on {withKeys} of # router task} other {Signing keys loaded on {withKeys} of # router tasks}}
ext.identityKeys.reason.noFreshTask: No router task has reported in the last 15 minutes, so the console cannot confirm that the keys are loaded. Check on the Health page that the router is running.
ext.identityKeys.reason.partial: Not every running router task has reported in the last 15 minutes, or the number of running tasks could not be read, for example during a deploy. Try again in a few minutes.
ext.identityKeys.reason.notConfigured: Router task {task} has no identity configured, so it cannot check x-api-key. Check the router stack identity settings.
ext.identityKeys.reason.taskWithoutKeys: Router task {task} has not loaded the signing keys. Try again in a minute. If it does not change, check the hourly key sync (jwks-sync) in the router stack.
models.title: Models
models.description: Every model this deployment knows in {region}: its state, where each value comes from, its price and whether the router may call it. Only confirmed models enter the price catalog and the model pools.
models.catalog.source.bundled: Shipped with this deployment (no catalog has been published yet)
models.universe.count: {count, plural, one {# model the router may call} other {# models the router may call}}
models.refresh.running: Refresh running. This page updates when it finishes.
models.empty: No models yet. The deploy writes the shipped models to catalog/models.json.
models.excluded.help: Curated exclusions: refreshes never add these ids and the router never routes to them.
models.filter.search: Find a model id or name
models.col.price: List price per 1M tokens (input / output / cache read)
models.reason.not-offered: no longer offered in this Region
models.missed: {count, plural, one {Missing from the latest refresh} other {Missing from the last # refreshes}} (retired after 3)
models.lifecycle.legacy.help: Bedrock marks this model LEGACY. It still serves requests and stays in the catalog; plan a replacement.
models.grant.adding.help: The model is being added to the catalog and granted to the router; this usually takes under a minute.
models.grant.base.help: In the deploy's allowed models (parameter allowedModelUniverse). Only a CDK deploy removes it.
models.grant.notInCatalog.help: Confirmed, but the price catalog in force does not include it: the Region does not offer it, or the last refresh left it out (see its notices). The router cannot call it until a refresh publishes it.
models.grant.none.help: Confirmed with the shipped models but not granted in this deployment. Grant access to let the router call it.
models.grant.done: {model} is granted. Every router task can call it within 60 seconds.
models.source.label: Source: {source}
models.confirm.title: Confirm {model}?
models.confirm.body: Confirming starts a catalog refresh: the model is added to the catalog and then granted to the router, usually within a minute. After that it can be used in the model pools, and callers can pin it.
models.confirm.grantBody: {model} is confirmed and in the catalog, but not granted in this deployment. Granting lets every router task call it within 60 seconds.
models.confirm.problems: This model cannot be confirmed yet:
models.confirm.rule.needs-price: It has no price: add a Price List SKU or a model-card price.
models.confirm.rule.unclassified: Its family is unknown: set the family first.
models.confirm.rule.retired: It is retired: the Region no longer offers it.
models.confirm.rule.metadata: Some of its metadata is not valid.
models.confirm.doneWaiting: {model} is confirmed. It is being added to the catalog and granted; this usually takes under a minute.
models.unconfirm.title: Unconfirm {model}?
models.unconfirm.body: The model goes back to pending and leaves the next catalog version. The router stops routing to it first, and its access is removed about a minute later; requests that pin it then get 400 pin-not-allowed.
models.unconfirm.policy: A model the routing configuration uses (a pool model, a failover, an observe default or the assessor model) cannot be unconfirmed: remove it on the Routing policy page first.
models.unconfirm.base: It stays granted: it is in the deploy's allowed models.
models.edit.title: Edit {model}
models.edit.help: Values you change are marked admin. Values from the API are read-only: every refresh sets them again.
models.edit.facts: From Bedrock and the price catalog
models.edit.conflict: This model changed while you were editing. Reload to see the current values, then make your change again.
models.edit.saveFirst: Save your changes before you confirm.
models.edit.field.family.help: Setting the family of an unclassified model makes it pending.
models.edit.field.contextWindowSource.he: Where the figure comes from, for example the model card. Optional.
models.edit.field.longContext.help: Above this many prompt tokens the whole request is priced at the long-context rate. Leave empty when the model has none.
models.edit.field.serviceTier.help: The Bedrock service tier the router asks for on Chat Completions and Responses when the client sends none. A service_tier from the client is kept. Flex costs less, and some models are served only on flex; priority costs more. Messages requests are not changed.
models.edit.field.cacheMinTokens: Minimum tokens per cache break point
models.edit.field.sku.help: Prices come from the AWS Price List rows of this model name.
models.edit.field.card.help: For models without a Price List SKU: the price on the Bedrock model card, USD per 1M tokens.
models.edit.field.cardTier.help: Optional. Without it the catalog uses the documented multiplier (flex ×0.5, priority ×1.75) and names it in the price source.
models.edit.error.nonNegativeInt: Enter a whole number, 0 or more.
models.edit.error.price: Enter a price of 0 or more.
models.edit.error.belowWindow: Must be below the context window.
models.edit.error.ttls: Choose at least one TTL when caching is on.
models.edit.error.defaultTtl: The default TTL must be one of the TTLs.
models.edit.error.skuName: Enter the model name as the Price List shows it.
models.edit.error.skuPrefix: The mantle scheme needs a usage-type prefix.
models.field.notInCatalog: Not in the current catalog version
models.addModal.title: Add a model
models.addModal.body: Adds a model id the Region offers that the refresh did not add by itself, for example a geographic inference profile. Its metadata comes from a template, and it stays pending until you confirm it.
models.addModal.field.help: The Bedrock model or inference profile id, as the Bedrock console shows it.
models.addModal.invalid: Use letters, digits and . : _ - only (3 to 200 characters).
models.refreshModal.title: Refresh the catalog now
models.refreshModal.body: Reads the Region's prices and models from AWS and publishes a new catalog version when something changed. It runs in the background and takes about a minute.
models.refreshModal.acceptIncomplete.hel: Use this when the last refresh stopped because the Region's list missed more than 20 % of the confirmed models, and those models really are gone. The refresh then treats them as no longer offered.
models.refreshModal.resume.help: After a rollback, refreshes keep the version you rolled back to and hold new prices. Tick this to publish the current prices again.
models.refreshModal.started: Refresh started. This page updates when it finishes.
catalog.notices.none: No notices from the latest refresh.
catalog.outcome.blocked: Not published: see the blocking notices
catalog.notice.policy-model-missing: {model} is used by the routing policy but is missing from the new catalog, so nothing was published. Remove it from the policy, or confirm it again.
catalog.notice.policy-model-legacy: {model} is used by the routing policy and is LEGACY in this Region. It still serves requests; replace it in the policy.
catalog.notice.model-legacy: {model} is LEGACY in this Region. It stays in the catalog.
catalog.notice.model-excluded: {model} is confirmed but the refresh left it out of the catalog. Check its price.
catalog.notice.model-pending: {model} waits for you to confirm it.
catalog.notice.model-unclassified: {model} has an unknown family. Set its family, then confirm it.
catalog.notice.listing-incomplete: The Region's model list missed {count, plural, one {# confirmed model} other {# confirmed models}} offered last time, so nothing was changed or published. If they really are gone, refresh again and accept the removals.
catalog.notice.listing-incomplete-accept: An admin accepted that {count, plural, one {# confirmed model is} other {# confirmed models are}} missing from the Region's model list.
catalog.notice.update-held: The catalog was rolled back, so this refresh did not publish the changes it found ({count, plural, one {# model} other {# models}}). Review them and resume updates when you are ready.
catalog.changes.alert: Price alert: a price moved by more than {threshold} %, or a price appeared or disappeared.
catalog.versions.description: The last 10 published versions, newest first. A version never changes once published; a rollback points the router back to an older one.
catalog.versions.none: No catalog has been published yet. The router uses the catalog shipped with this deployment ({version}).
catalog.versions.summary: {prices, plural, one {# price} other {# prices}} · {added} added · {removed} removed
catalog.versions.noChangeLog: No change log (for example the version a deploy published).
catalog.versions.paused: Automatic publishing is paused: the catalog was rolled back. Refreshes hold new prices until an admin resumes updates.
catalog.rollback.title: Roll back the price catalog to {version}?
catalog.rollback.body: The router, the console and usage pricing use version {version} again within 60 seconds. No version is changed or deleted.
catalog.rollback.pause: Automatic publishing pauses after a rollback: daily and manual refreshes hold new prices until an admin refreshes with “Resume updates after a rollback”.
catalog.rollback.done: The price catalog points to {version} again.
catalog.error.catalog-unavailable: The model catalog cannot be read: this deployment has no dynamic catalog, or catalog/models.json is missing. Redeploy the router stack.
catalog.error.conflict: Someone else changed the models or the catalog while you were saving. Reload, check their change and try again.
catalog.error.model-not-confirmable: This model cannot be confirmed yet. Fix the problems listed for it.
catalog.error.model-state: Retired and unclassified models cannot be unconfirmed: the catalog refresh manages these states.
catalog.error.model-exists: This model is already listed, or it is an excluded model.
catalog.error.model-not-offered: The latest capture shows that the Region does not offer this id. Check the id, or run a refresh first.
catalog.error.snapshot-unavailable: There is no usable capture of the Region's models yet. Run a refresh, then add the model.
catalog.error.rollback-unavailable: There is no older catalog version to roll back to.
catalog.error.invoke-failed: The change is saved, but the catalog function could not be started. Try the action again.
catalog.error.model-in-policy: This model is used by the routing configuration (a pool model, a failover, an observe default or the assessor model), so it cannot be unconfirmed. Remove it on the Routing policy page first.
catalog.error.catalog-held: The catalog is held after a rollback, so a newly confirmed model cannot be published. Resume updates first (a refresh with “Resume updates after a rollback”), then confirm again.
catalog.error.rollback-invalid: The configuration in force does not pass with this catalog version, so the router would reject it. Fix the problems below first, or roll back to another version.
catalog.router.catalog-rejected: The router rejected a catalog version and kept the previous one.
catalog.router.absent: No catalog is published; the router uses the one shipped with the deployment.
catalog.router.version-absent: The catalog version file is missing.
catalog.router.catalog-invalid: The catalog version file is not valid.
catalog.router.version-mismatch: The version file names another version than the pointer.
catalog.router.catalog-region: The catalog is for another Region.
catalog.router.boot-config-invalid: At startup the active config did not pass with this catalog.
catalog.router.document-invalid: The active routing policy does not pass with this catalog.
catalog.router.assessor-invalid: The assessor settings do not pass with this catalog.
catalog.router.engine-failed: The router could not build its routing engine with this catalog.
policy.pools.modelsHint: Only confirmed models the router may call are listed. New and pending models are on the Models page.
policy.pools.modelsWaiting: {count, plural, one {# model waits} other {# models wait}} for an admin on the Models page.
